findings.issue: [P2] CHANGELOG.md manually edited in violation of CLAUDE.md convention
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md states explicitly: 'Do NOT manually edit `CHANGELOG.md` or `README.md`. After all code changes are finalized, run `/update-documentation` to generate documentation updates.' This changeset directly modifies CHANGELOG.md (57 lines added) rather than generating it via the `/update-documentation` command. The exact rule violated is: 'Do NOT manually edit `CHANGELOG.md` or `README.md`.'
findings.recommendation: Revert the manual CHANGELOG.md edits and run `/update-documentation` to regenerate the changelog from the code changes.

findings.issue: [P2] write_runs_log_entry default command fallback is 'self_learning' but main loop calls emit no explicit command
findings.explanation: The new `write_runs_log_entry` function defaults `command` to `${LAST_CLAUDE_COMMAND:-self_learning}` when no 4th argument is supplied. The patch explicitly passes `"plan_execute"` to the `spurious_complete` callsite but leaves all other main-loop callsites (max_iterations, context_limit, ghost_loop_abort, completed, in_progress, error) without an explicit command argument. `LAST_CLAUDE_COMMAND` is only populated by `record_claude_session_id()`, which is called in the review/fix section with `"code_review"`. On fresh starts before any review runs, `LAST_CLAUDE_COMMAND` is empty (`""`) and the fallback `"self_learning"` is used for these plan_execute-context writes — making them indistinguishable from self-learning events in Datadog joins by command (PRD-254 attribution discipline). The CHANGELOG's intent is that main loop iterations carry `command="plan_execute"`.
findings.recommendation: Either pass `"plan_execute"` explicitly to all main-loop `write_runs_log_entry` callsites, or call `record_claude_session_id "$effective_workdir" "plan_execute" "$session_id"` in the main Claude invocation section so `LAST_CLAUDE_COMMAND` is set correctly before these writes execute.

findings.issue: [P2] emit_perf_event PERF_V2 path exits script via set -e if json_line is empty
findings.explanation: The new PERF_V2 block inside `emit_perf_event` does `json_line=$(echo "$json_line" | jq -c --arg command ... '. + {command:$command}')` (patch lines 492-494). When `json_line` is an empty string, `echo "" | jq -c '...'` exits non-zero (jq parse error on empty input). Because run-loop.sh runs under `set -euo pipefail`, this command-substitution assignment triggers an exit of the entire loop script. The pre-patch behavior was `echo "" >> "$perf_file"` which harmlessly wrote an empty line. A caller that passes an empty string to `emit_perf_event` — possible if an upstream `$(jq -n -c ...)` call fails in an env where `set -e` does not abort the outer assignment — would silently succeed before this change but terminate the loop after it.
findings.recommendation: Guard the jq call: `if [[ -n "$json_line" ]]; then json_line=$(echo "$json_line" | jq -c ...); fi` to make the PERF_V2 path fail-open consistent with the rest of the telemetry design.
